Appearance:
 Shri Rishi Tiwari - advocate for the petitioner.

Shri Anand Bhatt - Govt. Advocate for the respondent/St
 Order
Heard and perused the record.

2. This is second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail relating to Crime No.237/2024, dated (not mentioned)
registered at Police Station-Mahakal, District-Ujjain (M.P) for the offence under Sections 420, 34 of IPC, 1860.
The applicant is in custody since 11.07.2024.

Earlier application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 23.07.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.30348/2024.
3.

Allegation against the applicant is that he is involved in the aforesaid offence wherein main accused Mandakini Puri @ Mamta Joshi, who happens to be Mahamandleshwar of the institution has committed forgery of Rs. 8,80,000/- and the said amount has been deposited in the account of present applicant.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26584 2 MCRC-39338-2024 4.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case.

Earlier application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 23.07.2024 Ashvini Kumar Choudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128971119/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applicant is implicated only on the basis of memo of statement of main accused Mahamandleshwar Mandakini Puri.
It is alleged that main accused Mandakini Puri has received an amount of Rs.8.80 lakhs through applicant's account, this fact has also come in her memorandum of statement.
Main accused Mandakini Puri has already been released on bail after depositing Rs.4.40 lakhs.

Though the applicant has not received any money and applicant's bank account is alleged to have been operated by main accused Mandakini Puri, even then the applicant is ready to deposit Rs.4.40 lakhs 50% of the total amount in two installments.
The applicant is in custody since 11.07.2024.
Final conclusion of trial will take a sufficient long time.

Under these circumstances,
counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
5. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application.

6. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case and the applicant is ready to deposit Rs.4.40 lakhs, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant may be released on bail.

Consequently without commenting on the merits of the case, the bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed under the following conditions:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26584 3 MCRC-39338-2024 i. Subject to deposit before the Trial Court an amount of Rs.2,20,000/-
by the applicant at the time of furnishing the bail bond and Trial Court shall open an FD of the aforesaid amount in a Nationalized Bank.
ii.
Remaining Rs.2,20,000/- shall be deposited by the applicant within a period of three months from the date of releasing of the applicant.

iii. Applicant shall furnish a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only)
with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that she shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
iv.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE sumathi Ashvini Kumar Choudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128971119/
